summary: Thirteen court orders that the records knew only from news, trackers or party filings were located by an external retrieval with copies on court-record hosts. Research subagents opened the orders (storage.courtlistener.com RECAP copies, court sites, Justia, govinfo and copies of filed orders posted by state attorneys general or counsel; mirror and messaging-channel copies were rejected), and two independent reviewers re-opened the deciding copies and rewrote the 12 affected records. One stage changed: c05-24 (merit-based immigration and the diversity lottery) moved from in_progress to blocked with its earned progress of 25 kept, because the executive diversity visa steps that earned that progress were vacated for FY2026 subclasses (2026-08-28), rescinded by the State Department's own cable (2026-09-10) and enjoined as to DV-2027 registration (S.D. Cal., 2026-10-14). Corrections: the First Circuit's 2026-09-24 judgment in the HUD Continuum of Care appeals vacated the district court judgment on waiver of the notice-and-comment claim, not on the merits (c15-03); the Texas v. DOJ judgment of 2026-06-22 both vacates and permanently enjoins the 2024 EOIR administrative closure rule (c05-30); the Flores monitor orders are dated 2026-08-17 (c05-22); the third ruling on CFPB funding is State of New York v. Vought (D. Or.) of 2026-09-25 (c27-01); the 2026-09-22 District of Columbia ruling vacated EPA's program-wide Solar for All elimination decision rather than individual grant terminations (c13-07); the Section 301 forced-labor tariff suit was filed by 23 states and two governors (c26-01). Court status was added or re-dated on several records from opened orders. Counts: in_progress 208, blocked 18; 115 in effect of 627 counted.
title: Court-record pass over 12 records
